subject: SLA conversion options for committed volume — credits, rollover & conversion path
messages:
From: Elena Park <elena.park@acmedata.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Cc: procurements@acmedata.com
Date: Wed, 28 Mar 2028 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Converting unused SLA credits — options?

Hi Laura,

Quick question from the commercial team after our renewal review: Acme is looking to simplify how we consume the SLA / premium support credits we committed to last year. We have a left-over bucket from Q4 and would like to explore three options: (A) rollover to next quarter, (B) convert unused credits into a discount on token-based consumption, or (C) convert to a small retained on-call block (hours/month).

Can you outline what conversion paths Redwood supports, what conversion ratios you recommend, and whether any of these require an MSA amendment? We need a commercial working session next week to finalize the amendment language.

Thanks — Elena
Elena Park
Head of Cloud Procurement, Acme Data
[Attachment: usage_summary_Q4.pdf (application/pdf)]

From: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
To: Elena Park <elena.park@acmedata.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 29 Mar 2028 09:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Converting unused SLA credits — options?

Hi Elena — thanks for the clear set of options. We can support all three conversion paths with some guardrails: 1) Rollover: up to 25% of unused credits may roll over one quarter; larger rollovers on a case-by-case basis during renewals. 2) Conversion-to-consumption-discount: we typically convert SLA-credit value to a token-level rebate using a blended exchange rate (see proposal below). 3) Convert-to-retainer-hours: credits can be converted to a dedicated monthly on-call block; conversion is subject to minimums and lead time.

I attached two scenarios (low / high) in the spreadsheet and sketched an amendment paragraph that limits rollovers to one quarter and allows conversion during renewal windows only. High-level proposal: convert $1 of SLA credit to a 0.9¢ per-1k-token discount (example numbers in the sheet) or to 2 hours of named on-call triage for every $500 of credit.

Could we do a 30-minute call next Tue (4/2) 10am PT to walk through the spreadsheet and nail the wording for the MSA amendment? If that works I’ll loop in Legal to prepare a short addendum.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Sales Director, Enterprise Accounts | Redwood Inference
Mobile: +1 415-555-0123
[Attachment: sla-credit-scenarios.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)]

From: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 30 Mar 2028 11:21:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Acme — conversion options (need margin check)

Rishi / Ben — forwarding Acme’s ask. Fast turn here: they want us to be flexible across rollover / discount / retainer conversion. Pricing constraints are: preserve minimum recurring revenue, avoid channeling support load into cheaper credits, and keep SLA economics intact.

My suggested starter rules (so Legal/Finance have parameters):
- Rollovers: up to 25% automatically; exceptions require a renewal addendum.
- Conversion to token-discount: convert at 85–95% of dollar value depending on committed volume (higher commit => better rate). Example: $10k credit => ~0.9¢ per 1k-token discount applied to hosted API consumption for 3 months.
- Conversion to on-call retainer: $500 credit => 2 named hours/month for 3 months (minimum 6 months).

Can you run margin impact (Ben) and viability from an ops capacity perspective (Rishi)? If we approve, I'll propose the call for Tue 10am PT and ask Legal to draft the single-paragraph amendment.

—Laura

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 02 Apr 2028 08:47:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Fwd: Acme — conversion options (need margin check)

Laura / Rishi — quick summary after modeling:
- Rollover (25%) has negligible margin impact and is low risk operationally.
- Conversion to token-discount at 85% dollar-equivalent results in ~6% reduction to gross margin on expected volume for the 3-month window; acceptable for this strategic account if we cap to 3 months and require notice at renewal.
- Conversion to on-call retainer (2 hrs/$500) is thin margin but manageable if we require a 6-month minimum and named escalation contacts; we should also exclude high-severity incident handling unless they buy a higher support tier.

Recommendation: Offer a tiered conversion table in the amendment: up to $25k credits => rollover or convert-to-discount at 85%, $25k–$100k => 90%, >$100k => 95% (with legal signoff). For on-call conversion, require 6-month minimum and scoping in SOW.

I’ll join the Tue 10am PT call and bring the modeled numbers and the simple amendment language.

Cheers,
Ben Carter
Principal, Commercial Operations | Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 02 Apr 2028 15:34:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Converting unused SLA credits — options? (Summary + meeting invite)

Elena — thanks for the quick turn. Per internal alignment we propose the following for the working session:
- Proposed paths: 1) Auto-rollover up to 25% for one quarter, 2) Convert credits to hosted-token discount using tiered exchange (85% / 90% / 95% by bucket), 3) Convert to named on-call retainer (2 hrs per $500) with 6-month minimum and SOW.
- Limits: Conversions available during renewal windows or via mutual written amendment; token-discount applies for 3 months from conversion date.
- Next steps: 30-minute working session Tue 4/2 10:00–10:30 PT. I’ve attached the scenarios spreadsheet and a one-paragraph amendment draft to speed Legal review.

Meeting invite sent. Looking forward to finalizing language.

Warm regards,
Laura Bennett
